Table 1 indicates model-predicted node states that when established, can make Alpelisib treatment less effective in ER+ cells. We translate the model-indicated normalized values of Proliferation for the various interventions into comparative statements about Proliferation. We describe the experiments cited in support of each model result.

The model results are supported by experiments reported in PMID 27604488, in which they overexpressed constitutively active PIM1 and PIM2 in multiple cell lines and observed decreased response to Alpelisib (BYL719) treatment.

The model results are supported by PMID 23903756, which reports that inducing mTORC1 activity with IGF1 or NRG1 limits the reduction in cell numbers induced by Alpelisib in multiple cell lines. Specific experiments on MCF7 cells reported in PMID 23903756 are included in the context of the TM model.
The model results are supported by PMID 33685991, which reports that TSC2 inhibition confers resistance to Alpelisib treatment in MCF7 and T47D cells.

The model results are indirectly supported by experiments reported in PMID 21368164, which find that in multiple cell lines combining Alpelisib with  inhibition of HER3 or HER2 is more effective than Alpelisib alone.
The model results are supported by experiments reported in PMID 25002028, which find that cell lines resistant to Alpelisib (BYL719) treatment have high RB phosphorylation levels.
The model results are indirectly supported by PMID 27974663, which reports that inhibition of MCL1 synergizes with inhibition of PI3K or mTORC1.
The model results are supported by PMID 27604488, which reports that breast cancer cells with high AKT expression are resistant to PI3K inhibition.

The model results are supported by PMID 33685991, which finds that knockouts that lead to mTORC1 activation confer resistance to Alpelisib treatment. It is known that PRAS40 inhibition causes mTORC1 activation.
The model results are supported by experiments reported in PMID 28561737, which find that PIM2 leads to the inhibition (by phosphorylation) of BAD, and confers resistance to PI3K inhibition.

The effectiveness of combining Alpelisib with Everolimus is supported by PMID 23903756, which reports that in multiple cell lines combined inhibition of PI3K and mTORC1 is more effective than PI3K inhibition alone, and affects both proliferation and apoptosis.
The effectiveness of combined inhibition of PI3K and CDK4/6 in decreasing proliferation is supported by experiments in PMID 25002028 in multiple cell lines.
